comparator.academicYear: Indicative prospectus pathway: 2027–2028 year 1, 2028–2029 year 2 and 2029–2030 year 3
comparator.sourceNotes: The settled illustrative 180-EC French pathway is preserved: twelve required 5-EC first-year courses; six required 5-EC second-year courses and two restricted 15-EC Faculty of Arts minors; and third-year required francophone-university study 15 EC, professional-world course 5 EC, free choices 30 EC and thesis 10 EC. Zero-credit mentoring and language testing remain excluded. Additional programme-specific minor options remain optional and are not instantiated as mandatory major content. Checked 13 October 2026 against the official overview and three year pages. Their current labels are 2027–2028, 2028–2029 and 2029–2030 respectively; this corrects stale year-three source metadata, not any component, status or credit weight. The French direction within Romance Languages and Cultures is explicit. The public pages are provisional prospectus information, not a finalized external schedule for the Fall 2026 UCR cohort.

alternatives.concept: Study literary and visual expression through text analysis, film, art and museums, alongside cultural history and qualitative social inquiry. Two politics courses examine European and international institutions. This related-fields programme develops cultural interpretation; it provides neither French proficiency and translation nor a sustained francophone regional curriculum.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All formal prerequisites and exact workbook terms pass. Literary and rhetorical foundations precede stylistics/creative work and advanced interpretation; film introduction precedes documentary and adaptation; art introduction precedes museums and art historiography; sociology precedes qualitative inquiry; modern history precedes empire and the research seminar. African Art is assigned to its sole cohort offering in 2028h1, and the final literary/art-historiography courses to their actual 2029h1 offerings. No advisory progression signal is promoted into an invented prerequisite.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One complete related-fields cultural response is defensible. Literary/art/cultural-history interests are substantively represented by the completed core; another label does not establish a different curriculum. The first additional language-science concept fails: Psycholinguistics after its brain/behaviour gateway and stylistics provide only limited language-processing/text-analysis contributions, with no French proficiency, structure, acquisition sequence or sustained multilingualism study. Legal/administrative translation was assessed separately: EU/public/private law and Dutch can supply discrete domain knowledge, but the workbook contains no French language or translation methods; expanding law does not implement this direction. The France/Europe/international-organisations interest has two specific core courses; no evidence establishes an additional complete international-politics route with the required distinct target-grounded course consequences. Stop at one, without attempting a third. Professional qualification is not used as the academic failure criterion.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both directly develop literary/textual analysis; the UCR course is comparative and English-medium rather than French textual work.

notes.text: Radboud combines French proficiency, linguistics and francophone literature/culture with translation, required francophone-university study and a thesis. This UCR programme studies related literary, visual and historical questions through literature, film, art, history and social inquiry, with European/international institutional contributions. It does not provide French proficiency, French–Dutch translation, required francophone immersion or a sustained francophone regional curriculum.
